around.headline: 3 students among 5 killed in a bus crash on the Goa-to-Bengaluru route
around.summary: A bus travelling from Goa to Bengaluru crashed, killing five people including three students, according to today's report. If you're booking an overnight or long-distance bus, favour operators with named drivers and recent safety ratings over the cheapest fare.

around.headline: 60-year-old landlord accused of sexually harassing a student tenant in a rented Bengaluru flat
around.summary: A landlord has been accused of sexually harassing a student living in his rented flat, per today's report. When flat-hunting, avoid solo viewings with an unfamiliar landlord — bring a friend or do a video walkthrough first, and note that landlords have no legal right to enter your rented space without notice.

around.headline: Weekend rush and rain choke Outer Ring Road again, heavy showers disrupting tech corridors today
around.summary: ORR and the tech-corridor stretches are reported slow again today as rain combines with the Friday weekend rush. If your route runs through ORR, Sarjapur or the Whitefield/Outer Ring corridor this evening, leave earlier than usual or check live traffic before you set out.

around.headline: Bengaluru's new parking rules aim to clear traffic chokepoints at notorious junctions
around.summary: New parking regulations are being rolled out with the goal of easing congestion at some of the city's worst junctions. Watch for new no-parking signage near junctions you regularly pass — enforcement typically follows soon after such rules are announced.

around.headline: Bengaluru airport to charge arriving passengers a User Development Fee from September 1, departure UDF cut to Rs 300
around.summary: From September 1, arriving passengers at Bengaluru airport will also be charged a User Development Fee, while the fee for departing passengers is being cut to Rs 300. If you're flying out of or into Bengaluru after that date, factor the fee into your ticket cost.

around.headline: Tata Motors to hike car and SUV prices by up to Rs 25,000 from September 2026
around.summary: Tata Motors has announced a price increase of up to Rs 25,000 on its cars and SUVs starting next month. If you're close to finalising a Tata purchase, booking before September could save you the hike.

around.headline: Two ships with 22 Indian crew hijacked by armed pirates off Yemen and Somalia
around.summary: Pirates have hijacked two ships carrying 22 Indian crew members off the coast of Yemen and Somalia, according to today's report. It's a reminder of the real risk Indian seafarers still face on this route, which also affects shipping insurance costs and delivery times for goods.

street_smart.title: You get off a late train or bus at a Bengaluru railway station and grab idlis and a cut onion from a stall for a quick bite before heading to work. Halfway through, you notice something hard and slick mixed into the idli, and the onion looks faintly discoloured. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real incident: Karnataka food safety raids at railway stations found plastic mixed into idlis and fungal onions being served at stalls (Times of India). Food/consumer safety hasn't been used as a street-smart topic in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: You're hungry, in a hurry to get to work, and the stall looked no different from any other you've eaten at. The stall owner is busy serving the next customer and hasn't noticed anything.

choices.text: Stop eating immediately, keep the food as evidence, and report it on the spot to the station manager or RPF, or call the railway helpline 139 — mention the stall by name or number and the time.
choices.feedback: Correct, and doing it immediately matters twice over: it stops you from eating more of something already flagged as unsafe by the very raids in today's news, and a same-day complaint with the stall identified is what lets RPF or FSSAI actually act on it, rather than it being one more shrug-and-move-on story. Railway helpline 139 logs complaints centrally and is meant exactly for this.

choices.text: Pick out the plastic, finish the rest since you already paid for it and you're running late, and forget about it.
choices.feedback: This is exactly what lets stalls like the ones in today's raids keep operating — a few rupees paid, no complaint filed, and the same fungal produce or contaminated batch served to the next hurried commuter. One visible piece of plastic in food also means you have no way of knowing what else made it into that batch; 'already paid for it' isn't a reason to keep eating something flagged as unsafe.

choices.text: Quietly throw the rest away and just avoid that stall yourself in future.
choices.feedback: Better than eating it, but it protects only you. The stall keeps serving the same food to everyone else, and without a complaint on record, no inspection gets triggered — which is exactly how these violations, like the ones raided today, go unnoticed for so long.

choices.text: Confront the stall owner loudly on the spot and demand a refund before deciding what else to do.
choices.feedback: A refund is a fair ask, but making it the whole response risks turning into a shouting match that gets you nothing beyond your money back, while the stall carries on afterward. Get the refund if it's offered, but still file the complaint with the station authorities — that's the step that actually leads to an inspection.

takeaways: If food from a stall looks or feels visibly off, stop eating it right away — don't finish it just because you already paid.
Report unsafe food at a railway station to the RPF/station manager or the railway helpline 139, and name the stall and time — that's what triggers an actual inspection.
A personal boycott of one stall protects only you; a filed complaint is what gets it checked and, if needed, shut down for everyone.

quiz.question: From what date will Bengaluru airport start charging a User Development Fee to arriving passengers too, per today's news?
quiz.why: The same change cuts the User Development Fee for departing passengers to Rs 300 — UDF is a per-passenger charge airports levy to fund infrastructure upgrades.

quiz.question: How much unaccounted cash did Bengaluru police seize from a car headed to Tamil Nadu, triggering an Income Tax department probe?
quiz.why: Cash seizures above certain thresholds during transit routinely get referred to the Income Tax department to check whether the money is accounted for and taxed.

quiz.question: By how much is Tata Motors raising car and SUV prices from September 2026, per today's report?
quiz.why: Automakers often front-load price hikes to the start of a new month or fiscal period, so booking before the effective date can lock in the older price.

quiz.question: What is the minimum age to contest an election to the Lok Sabha, Parliament's lower house?
quiz.why: The minimum age is higher, at 30, to contest for the Rajya Sabha or a state's Vidhan Parishad (the upper houses).

quiz.question: Which organ in the human body primarily produces insulin?
quiz.why: Insulin regulates blood sugar; when the pancreas makes too little of it or the body resists its effect, the result is diabetes.
